Cyanobacteria are a group of autotrophic gram-negative bacteria of the phylum Cyanobacteriota that can obtain biological energy via oxygenic photosynthesis. Photosynthetic cyanobacteria dominated Precambrian shallow oceans for hundreds of millions of years. The great oxidation event transformed the atmosphere of the early Earth permanently.

My own analysis of these findings suggests a different interpretation. The evidence points toward multiple independent origins of oxygenic photosynthesis. However, the fossil record remains incomplete and contested among researchers. Future work should combine genomic and geological approaches carefully.
